clue.text: Before the consummation of love Cupid pretended to show up

parts.note: a putto is a chubby winged cherub in art, a little Cupid figure
to sham is to pretend

indicators.note: a consummation is a completion or ending, so only the closing letter of the next word is wanted

parts.note: the final letter of love

explanation.surface: A romantic scene in which Cupid is caught faking it just before the lovers finally come together.
explanation.walkthrough: A putto, the chubby cherub of Renaissance painting, is a crossword stand-in for Cupid. 'Before' only sets the order of the last two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To show someone up is to outshine them embarrassingly, which is exactly what putting them to shame means.

clue.text: A capital fellow who 15

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the French capital city
second meaning: the Trojan prince who abducted Helen, with 15 read as its answer

explanation.surface: A splendid chap who carried someone off.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 15 as its answer, kidnapped: Paris of Troy kidnapped Helen of Sparta, starting the Trojan War. 'capital' also hints at the old British praise word for excellent.
explanation.definitionFit: The French capital shares its name with the Trojan prince who carried off Helen from Sparta.

clue.text: Brownie points given thus as profit

definitions.meaning: first meaning: merit points awarded for behaving well, handed to the well-behaved
second meaning: on the credit side, in gain

explanation.surface: A Brownie leader hands out merit points as a reward.
explanation.walkthrough: Brownies are the junior branch of the Girl Guides; points go to the good ones. 'Brownie points' is also the idiom for credit earned by pleasing someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Being so much to the good means ending up ahead financially, with a net gain or surplus.

clue.text: Conversely, hath not done her wrong

indicators.note: done wrong means badly put together, so the letters before it are out of order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned protest: on the contrary, he has not wronged her.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase introduces an opposing point of view, just as the single adverb conversely does.

clue.text: Fish taken to wharf

parts.note: had is a past form of have, to take
a dock is a wharf for ships

explanation.surface: A catch is landed at the quayside.
explanation.definitionFit: The haddock is a North Atlantic food fish related to the cod, so it is a specific example of a fish.

clue.text: Thousand Island — a source of dressings to beguile

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand
an isle is an island
taken as written

indicators.note: a source is where something begins, so only the opening letter of the next word counts

parts.note: the initial letter of dressings

explanation.surface: Thousand Island is named as one of the salad dressings that tempts the diner.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads Thousand Island as the salad dressing; it splits into a numeral and a word for an island.
explanation.definitionFit: To beguile someone is to charm or trick them into a false belief, which is to deceive them.

clue.text: Atlas section including Afghanistan starts here

indicators.note: starts points to the opening letter of each of the preceding words in turn

parts.note: the initial letters of these four words

explanation.surface: A reader thumbing through an atlas finds where the pages on Afghanistan begin.
explanation.walkthrough: The four words both supply the letters and describe the answer: the continental section of an atlas containing Afghanistan.
explanation.definitionFit: Afghanistan lies in the continent of Asia, which gets its own chapter of maps in any world atlas.

clue.text: Fauns revel in chaos

indicators.note: revellers cavort wildly, so the letters are thrown into disarray

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Woodland goat-men party riotously in a scene of disorder.
explanation.walkthrough: SNAFU began as military slang, an acronym for 'situation normal, all fouled up'.
explanation.definitionFit: A snafu is a muddled, chaotic situation in which everything has gone wrong, so it stands for confusion and mess.

clue.text: Dump in terminals down under

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: anodes are positive electrical terminals
a tip is a rubbish dump

explanation.surface: Rubbish piles up at the ends of the line in Australia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terminals' suggests the ends of a railway line; here it means electrodes. A tip is the everyday British word for a rubbish dump.
explanation.definitionFit: The Antipodes is the British name for Australia and New Zealand, opposite Britain on the globe, colloquially down under.

clue.text: Cast adrift, swans say they have no home

indicators.note: cast in the sense of thrown about, so the letters that follow land in a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Swans set loose on the water lament that they have nowhere to live.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cast adrift' reads as a single phrase, but 'Cast' alone signals the anagram and 'adrift' is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Waifs and strays are homeless people or animals, so the phrase names those lacking anywhere to live.

clue.text: Turned detonator over? That's not on

indicators.note: something knocked over lands in disorder, so the remaining letters are rearranged
not on says a pair of letters spelling that little word must be taken away

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone flips a detonator upside down and is told sharply that it's unacceptable behaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing ON from DETONATOR leaves DETATOR, which rearranges to ROTATED. 'That's not on' sounds like a reprimand but is the deletion instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: Something rotated has been turned around on an axis, so the past participle matches turned.

clue.text: As a remedy for leaks, man infiltrates gang

indicators.note: to infiltrate is to get inside a group, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a set is a group or clique
a man's name

explanation.surface: A spy-story line: a plumber goes undercover inside a criminal gang to stop the leaks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'man' stands for any man's name the setter likes; 'leaks' sounds like secrets passed on, but it means drips.
explanation.definitionFit: A sealant is a substance applied to stop leaks, so it is described by its purpose as a fix for them.

clue.text: Deserve to get training as a docker

indicators.note: training reshapes something, so these letters are worked into a new form

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A trainee earns their place on the waterfront by learning the dock work.
explanation.definitionFit: A stevedore is a labourer who loads and unloads ships, the same job as a docker or longshoreman.

clue.text: The fellow behind a dowdy woman

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fellow
the rump is the backside

explanation.surface: A man trails along after a drab, unfashionable woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'behind' looks like a preposition placing the fellow, but it is a noun meaning backside.
explanation.definitionFit: A frump is a woman who dresses in an old-fashioned, unattractive way, so dowdy describes her exactly.

clue.text: Strong drink

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a dark heavy beer

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as one phrase about a powerful drink; split it into two separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means sturdy and solidly built, while the noun is a dark beer brewed with roasted barley, such as Guinness.

clue.text: Skin a fish — one still growing

parts.note: to strip is to peel off a covering
the ling is a long fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: A cook prepares a fish that is still young.
explanation.definitionFit: A stripling is a youth not yet fully grown, a young lad on the way to manhood.

clue.text: Child slept for a while. — that's novel!

parts.note: a kid is a child
to nap is to sleep briefly

explanation.surface: A parent remarks that their child taking a nap is a real novelty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' seems to mean new or surprising; it is the definition, Robert Louis Stevenson's 1886 adventure story.
explanation.definitionFit: Kidnapped is the Stevenson adventure book about David Balfour, so it is an example of a novel.

clue.text: Strange events gave rise to flower power

parts.note: pH, the acidity scale, is named for the power of hydrogen

indicators.note: in a down entry rising means reading upwards, from bottom to top

parts.note: the anemone is a flower

explanation.surface: Something odd happened that sparked the hippie movement of the sixties.
explanation.walkthrough: Flower power was the 1960s hippie slogan. Here 'flower' is ANEMONE rising, so ENOMENA, and 'power' comes first as PH.
explanation.definitionFit: Phenomena are remarkable or unusual occurrences, so the plural matches strange events.

clue.text: Memorable as a joyful occasion for the florid Latvian king

parts.note: a florid face is flushed red
a Lett is a Latvian person
ER, from Latin Edwardus Rex, is King Edward's cipher

explanation.surface: A happy day of celebration is held in honour of a ruddy-faced Baltic monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: A red-letter day is a special, happy one, from the old practice of marking feast days in red on calendars.

clue.text: Criminal often found in the bag

definitions.meaning: first meaning: rhyming slang for thief
second meaning: what fills a tea bag

explanation.surface: A crook is frequently caught, as the police say, in the bag.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney rhyming slang makes 'tea leaf' mean thief.
explanation.definitionFit: In London slang a thief is a tea-leaf, and leaves of tea are what teabags are filled with.

clue.text: Bones broken in big race …

indicators.note: something broken is smashed apart, so the letters are reassembled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A jockey suffers fractures in a major horse race.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a fall in a race, with 'Bones broken' read as one injury; 'broken' belongs with what follows.
explanation.definitionFit: The rib cage is the bony frame of ribs that protects the chest, so it is a set of bones.

clue.text: Adjust one's clothing

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to line up or arrange
second meaning: what a person wears

explanation.surface: A polite reminder to straighten your clothes before going out.
explanation.definitionFit: To dress troops is to align them properly, and a person's dress is the garments they have on.

clue.text: A proper church contains somewhere to sit

indicators.note: contains says the letters are held within the run of words just before it

parts.note: read across the join of the two words

explanation.surface: A well-ordered church naturally has pews for the congregation.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening 'A' only helps the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A perch is a place for a bird to rest, and loosely any high spot where someone settles.

clue.text: … racehorse gets up to go over it again

indicators.note: in a down entry getting up means reading upwards, bottom to top

parts.note: a pacer is a horse bred for harness racing

explanation.surface: Continuing the race story: the horse gets back up to run the course a second time.
explanation.definitionFit: To recap is to summarise points already made, so it means to repeat them briefly.

clue.text: Shot by mariner or good golfer

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the seabird killed in Coleridge's Rime of the Ancient Mariner
second meaning: a hole played three under par

explanation.surface: A shot is fired by a sailor, or played by a skilled golfer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shot' looks like a golf stroke but here means killed with a crossbow. The second definition is loose: the score is something a good golfer makes.
explanation.definitionFit: Coleridge's sailor kills the great seabird, and in golf the term means three strokes under par on one hole.

clue.text: Swell stuff, by the sound of it

indicators.note: points to a word that is spoken the same as the one meant

parts.note: serge is a hard-wearing twilled fabric, and stuff is an old word for woollen cloth

explanation.surface: Someone hears about something great and remarks that it sounds swell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swell' poses as the slang adjective for excellent; it is the noun or verb for a rising wave.
explanation.definitionFit: A surge is a sudden rise in the sea, just as a swell is a heaving rise of water.

clue.text: Joss-sticks make one's hackles rise

definitions.meaning: first meaning: perfumed material burned for its smell
second meaning, stressed on the second syllable: to anger

explanation.surface: Someone finds the smell of burning joss-sticks infuriating.
explanation.definitionFit: Joss-sticks are sticks of fragrant material burned in temples, and to enrage someone is to make them bristle with fury.

clue.text: Unprofessional game's over after a final move

parts.note: taken as written
checkmate is the last move of a chess game

indicators.note: turned over means the abbreviation is read from the other end

parts.note: RU is short for Rugby Union

explanation.surface: A chess match ends once the decisive move is played.
explanation.walkthrough: 'game's over' sounds like the end of play, but 'over' turns the game round and 'after' puts it at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: An amateur does something unpaid or without expert skill, so the word works as an adjective for unprofessional.

clue.text: Opening a love-feast? The opening's off

indicators.note: the first letter is removed, since the opening is taken off

parts.note: an agape is an early Christian fellowship meal of love

explanation.surface: Someone asks if a love-feast is opening, then learns the start has been called off.
explanation.walkthrough: The agape was a communal meal shared by early Christians, from the Greek for love. Dropping its first letter leaves GAPE.
explanation.definitionFit: A gape is a wide opening, such as the open mouth of a bird or a gap in something.

clue.text: Toiletry — a course to experience

parts.note: afters is British slang for the dessert course of a meal
to have a time is to experience it

explanation.surface: A grooming product sold as something to try out.
explanation.definitionFit: Aftershave is a scented lotion splashed on after shaving, one of the items kept in a toiletry bag.
